nodes.summary: Let $A$, $B$, $C$ be affinely independent points of the Euclidean plane and $P$ a point in the interior of the triangle $ABC$. Let $M$, $N$, $L$ be points on the lines $BC$, $AB$, $CA$ such that $PM \perp BC$, $PN \perp AB$ and $PL \perp CA$. Then, writing $XY$ for the distance between points $X$ and $Y$, we have $PA + PB + PC \ge 2(PM + PN + PL)$.
nodes.title: Erdős–Mordell inequality

nodes.summary: Writing $XY$ for the distance between points $X$ and $Y$, this is the assertion that for all affinely independent points $A$, $B$, $C$ of the Euclidean plane, every point $P$ in the interior of the triangle $ABC$, and all points $M$, $N$, $L$ on the lines $BC$, $AB$, $CA$ such that the lines $PM$, $PN$, $PL$ are perpendicular to $BC$, $AB$, $CA$ respectively, we have $PA + PB + PC \ge 2(PM + PN + PL)$.
nodes.title: Statement of the Erdős–Mordell inequality
